options.text: Its particles move freely in all directions with negligible attractions, so the gas spreads to fill the available space.
Its particles stay tightly packed in fixed positions, like particles in a solid rubber balloon skin.
The gas fills the room first, and that filling then causes its particles to begin moving freely.
The same explanation applies to the solid rubber balloon skin itself, not only to the helium gas.

stem:
Ira opens the valve of a helium party balloon in one corner of a closed classroom. Soon the helium spreads through the whole room and fills every part of the available space.

Why does this gas have no fixed shape or fixed volume?

teacher.key_rationale: In a gas, particles move freely with negligible attractions, so the gas has no fixed shape or volume and fills available space. Treating the gas like a solid, reversing cause and effect, or applying the rule to the rubber skin miss the hinge.
